decision_rationale: All three families are architecturally complete (H1/H2/H11 SUPPORTED: full descriptor-to-real-runtime path, policy round-trip, zero regressions) and each shows a real, separately-measured optimization effect in at least one clearly-defined domain (RMSNorm custom kernel vs torch.compile; LM-head real serving TPOT; MatMul INT8-packed-plus-codegen vs FP32). This alone would satisfy THREE_FAMILY_OPTIMIZATION_VALIDATED's literal bar. However, two real, honestly-measured negative/partial findings exist that the task explicitly requires not be blurred into an unqualified success: (1) RMSNorm's SELECTOR specifically does not beat a single well-chosen fixed block size on this shape sweep (H4 REJECTED -- the speedup credit belongs to the custom kernel, not shape-aware selection); (2) MatMul's unified selector achieves only 7-8/9 fidelity to the gated production selector, not 9/9 (H9 PARTIAL, Path B). Both are selector-accuracy nuances layered on top of otherwise-real custom-kernel/precision wins. Per the task's explicit instruction to separate selector accuracy from custom-kernel value from architecture completeness and to report negative results honestly, THREE_FAMILY_COMPLETE_MIXED_PERFORMANCE is the more precise choice: complete architecture, mixed (not uniformly clean) performance/fidelity picture.

Selector accuracy.LM-head: within 0.83% of direct E2E-8 at all batches
Selector accuracy.MatMul-Bias-ReLU: 7/9 fresh-run agreement with gated production selector (PARTIAL, known gap)

Framework/native baseline measured.RMSNorm: eager + torch.compile real; flashinfer attempted, unavailable on this GPU
Framework/native baseline measured.MatMul-Bias-ReLU: FP32 tiled (project's own always-legal baseline), real

Worst regression.RMSNorm: selector 6.6% slower than best fixed block at one shape
Worst regression.MatMul-Bias-ReLU: unified selector picks INT8 where production correctly falls back to FP32 at 2 tiny shapes

Dispatch overhead.MatMul-Bias-ReLU: ~3.05ms one-time selection (large but amortized to 0.135us cached), 1.55s one-time graph build

Production-path integration.RMSNorm: standalone (no separate 'production' RMSNorm path exists in this project outside this system)
Production-path integration.LM-head: YES, real OOT LogitsProcessor extension point, zero vLLM source patch
Production-path integration.MatMul-Bias-ReLU: reuses the real slice3c/portable_cpu_kernel_adapter production dispatch contract

Remaining gap.RMSNorm: selector value vs fixed block is neutral/negative on this shape domain
Remaining gap.MatMul-Bias-ReLU: stability/performance gate not integrated into the unified selector (Path B, explicit)

distinctions_required_by_task.rmsnorm_custom_kernel_speedup: 1.34x-2.98x vs torch.compile (the real fastest non-custom baseline)
distinctions_required_by_task.rmsnorm_selector_speedup_over_fixed_bloc: mean 0.986x (i.e. selector is ~1.4% SLOWER on average than a single well-chosen fixed block on this sweep) -- NOT a selector win
distinctions_required_by_task.lm_head_direct_gemv_optimization: -21.2%-ish TPOT at batch=2 (E2E-8 original) / -21.48% (this slice's fresh direct_e2e8-vs-baseline re-measurement)
distinctions_required_by_task.lm_head_unified_framework_preservation: unified selector within 0.83% of direct E2E-8 at every tested batch
distinctions_required_by_task.matmul_kernel_precision_speedup: 2.14x-14.06x vs FP32 fallback where INT8+packing+codegen is selected
distinctions_required_by_task.matmul_selector_fidelity_to_gated_produc: 7/9 (this slice's fresh run) / 8/9 (E2E-10's original run) -- NOT 9/9, explicit known gap
